t: Reimbursement to District of Columbia, benefit payments to White House Police and Secret Service forces: For an additional amount, fiscal year 1947, for “Reimbursement to District of Columbia, benefit payments to White House Police and Secret Service forces”, $16,000.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriation of funds to reimburse the District of Columbia for benefit payments. The tempting reading is that mentioning the District of Columbia (a non-federal/local entity) signals coordination, but it is only a payment recipient; no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: For an additional amount, fiscal year 1947, for “Reimbursement to District of Columbia, benefit payments to White House Police and Secret Service forces”, $16,000.

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple appropriation clause authorizing a specific sum of money for reimbursements and benefit payments. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties before a decision is made. The payment of benefits or reimbursement is an administrative action, not a participatory decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: Reimbursement to District of Columbia, benefit payments to White House Police and Secret Service forces: For an additional amount, fiscal year 1947, for “Reimbursement to District of Columbia, benefit payments to White House Police and Secret Service forces”, $16,000.

opus.w: This section only provides extra money for reimbursing the District of Columbia for benefit payments. It sets up no consultation, hearing, advisory body, comment period or right to sue. Naming the District of Columbia, a local government, does not make this participation, because the District takes no part in any federal decision.
opus.s: For an additional amount, fiscal year 1947, for “Reimbursement to District of Columbia, benefit payments to White House Police and Secret Service forces”, $16,000.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning.** Someone might read "Reimbursement to District of Columbia" as federal dealings with a local government. That reading fails. This is just an extra appropriation of money. No outside party is consulted, holds a hearing, gives advice or gets a right to sue before a federal decision is made.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriation clause authorizing funds for reimbursements and benefit payments. It does not require or recommend any form of participation by outside parties in federal decision-making. The recipients of the payments (White House Police and Secret Service) are federal employees or agents, and the District of Columbia is a local government entity receiving reimbursement, but there is no consultation, advisory role, or public input mechanism described.
qwen_chat.s: Reimbursement to District of Columbia, benefit payments to White House Police and Secret Service forces: For an additional amount, fiscal year 1947, for “Reimbursement to District of Columbia, benefit payments to White House Police and Secret Service forces”, $16,000.

It does not establish any mechanism for consultation, public comment, advisory boards with non-federal members, or rights to sue.
